session_dialogue.text: Hello. How are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit anxious today. I just got a notice about my insurance claim, and it's all a bit overwhelming.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like a lot to handle, but let's take it step by step. What specifically is making you feel anxious?
The insurance claim had an unexpected balance, and I feel like I messed up. I thought I was handling everything on my own, but now I'm worried I'm not capable.
That must be really stressful. It’s normal to feel overwhelmed when things don’t go as planned, but you’re doing your best, and that’s what matters.
I know I’m trying, but it’s hard not to feel like a failure when I mess up. I keep thinking I should have known better, and that I’m not really independent after all.
It’s okay to feel that way sometimes. But you’re not alone in this, and it doesn’t mean you’re not capable. You’re just human.
I guess I just feel so much pressure to be perfect. Every mistake feels like a sign that I’m not cut out for this.
That pressure to be perfect can be really heavy. It’s understandable to feel like a mistake means you’re not enough, but that doesn’t reflect who you are as a person.
I know, but it’s so hard to stop thinking that way. Every time something goes wrong, I feel like I’m failing myself and everyone who believes I can do this.
It’s tough when mistakes feel like they’re betraying the people who believe in you. But you’re allowed to struggle, and it doesn’t mean you’re failing anyone.
I just feel like I’m letting them down, even though I don’t want to be. It’s like every time I make a mistake, I’m proving I’m not strong enough.
It’s painful to feel like your mistakes are a reflection of your strength or worth. But your value isn’t tied to how well you handle every situation.
I know, but it feels like everything I do is being judged. Even when I try my best, I can’t shake the feeling that I’m not good enough.
It’s hard to feel like you’re always being judged, even when you’re doing your best. But your worth isn’t defined by others’ expectations or your own perfectionism.
I wish I could believe that. But every time I mess up, it feels like I’m confirming all the worst things I think about myself.
It’s understandable to feel like your mistakes are confirming your worst fears. But those thoughts don’t have to define your reality — they’re just part of the struggle.
I know, but it’s so hard to break free from those thoughts. They feel like they’re part of me, not just something I’m dealing with.
It’s hard to feel like those thoughts are part of you, but they’re not who you are — they’re just temporary patterns that can change with time and support.
I want to believe that, but it’s like I’m stuck in a loop. Every time I try to move forward, the same thoughts come back, and I feel like I’m not in control.
